:::{#thm-evidence-lower-bound-decomposition}
#### The log evidence is the ELBO plus a divergence

Let $\pf{x, z}$ and $q$ be as in @def-evidence-lower-bound.
Let $\pf{x} = \sum_z \pf{x, z}$ be the [evidence](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/bayesian-inference.html#def-marginal-likelihood) of the data,
also called its [marginal likelihood](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/bayesian-inference.html#def-marginal-likelihood).
The evidence is nonzero,
because a data value $x$ was observed.
Then the [logarithm](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-logarithm) of the evidence is the [ELBO](#def-evidence-lower-bound) of $q$
plus the [Kullback--Leibler divergence](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-kl-divergence) of $q$ from the [posterior](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/bayesian-inference.html#def-posterior):

$$\logf{\pf{x}} = \mathrm{ELBO}(q) + \kldivf{q}{\pf{\cdot \given x}}.$$

:::

::: proof

Let $z$ be a value with $q(z) > 0$.
Then $\pf{z \given x} \ne 0$,
and $\pf{x, z} = \pf{z \given x} \, \pf{x}$.
Apply $\logt$ to both sides and rearrange:

$$\logf{\pf{x}} = \logf{\pf{x, z}} - \logf{\pf{z \given x}}.$$

Add and subtract $\logf{q(z)}$ on the right:

$$\logf{\pf{x}} = \paren{\logf{\pf{x, z}} - \logf{q(z)}} + \paren{\logf{q(z)} - \logf{\pf{z \given x}}}.$$

Multiply both sides by $q(z)$,
then sum over the values $z$ with $q(z) > 0$.
The left side sums to $\logf{\pf{x}}$,
because $q$ sums to $1$:

$$\logf{\pf{x}} = \sum_z q(z) \paren{\logf{\pf{x, z}} - \logf{q(z)}} + \sum_z q(z) \paren{\logf{q(z)} - \logf{\pf{z \given x}}}.$$

The first sum is $\mathrm{ELBO}(q)$ by its definition.
The second sum is $\kldivf{q}{\pf{\cdot \given x}}$ by the definition of the divergence.

:::
